column8: Wed 18 Nov: store background for 3e on what a MAC is; the 99% is Denis and Macias's share of deals with any MAC clause (755 deals, 1998-2005), never the economy carve-out's figure in row 3; l.17's exits are for when the plan cannot be carried out (Q7b-033), not one party's exit against another.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e evaluation of l.17's shape: a MAC is a vague trigger plus a long exception list, l.17 a closed list of two events plus one ten-word carve-out; a spot check of the article's text did not reach the word counts (likely in its exhibits), so confirm before any figure; 3e needs the contrast in words, no figure.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e, the strongest frame for l.17's third sentence: the economy carve-out sits in nearly every large merger agreement, so a fall in the market is not one of them is standard practice; a spot check found 99% in the text only as Denis and Macias's share of deals with any MAC clause, so check the 99+% against the carve-out exhibit before printing it and never conflate the two; in words in 3e (density cut); never call l.17 a MAC clause.

Wed 18 Nov: store only; carve-outs spread from 18.33% of 1993 contracts (Gilson and Schwartz, also quoted by Subramanian and Petrucci, 83% by 2000) to nearly all by 2005; supports row 3, no report job of its own.

Wed 18 Nov: store; the CONFLICTING label compares two different carve-outs, the target's own share price (25%) and securities markets at large (over 80%), which row 7's clause lists separately: name which each figure counts and its sample ($100 million up against $1 billion up) before use; the usable point is pandemics going from 25% to 88% (lists grow after each surprise).

Wed 18 Nov: 3e; the critique column's line is the job: rates, currency and inflation are carved out of the reasons, never out of the results (yields set the bottom to January 2028; the Taiwan dollar and building costs call on her flexibility, Table 3 rows 6-7); beside Q7b-038; Akorn read in excerpts.
Wed 18 Nov: References or one 3e clause at most: a primary clause on EDGAR whose any decline, in and of itself, in the market price sits closest to l.17's words; never quoted at length (3e's budget).

Wed 18 Nov: 3e and Table 3 row 2: a deal clause looks through a price fall to its cause, while the plan watches no price, yield or rating, only whether a Treasury pays within five business days; the contrast is Keel's inference; row 37 merged here.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e: deals need a carve-back because a market fall can hit a target harder than its peers; the payments hold no shares, so l.17 needs none (NUMBERS 8p checked: VT worthless at the move, all ten paid, range $95,000); a new frame on Q109-032's deletion test; never protected from crashes.

Wed 18 Nov: store or one 3e clause at most: IBP calls a MAE a backstop for unknown events and kept a short-term hiccup out with no carve-out written; l.17 names known events in advance, which row 14 says more plainly.

Wed 18 Nov: store; an exit found after the fact is distrusted, beside Q7c-004 (Stanford named its trigger after the fall) and Q111-001; say l.17 was submitted 7 Nov 2026 (Sydney), before the first purchase in January 2027.
Wed 18 Nov: store or a 3e clause on how high the bar is; Hexion's never found and This is not a coincidence checked at source tonight; dated wording only (row 22).

Wed 18 Nov: store; checked at source tonight: the 32% is Huntsman's full-year 2008 EBITDA forecast ($879 million) against the forecast of the year before ($1.289 billion), not a forecast fall of 32% in earnings; reword as first-half EBITDA down 19.9% and its 2008 forecast cut 32%, in the verdict's claim 2 too.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e, why the two reasons can be checked by anyone: Hexion's strange animals against easily ascertainable objective facts, checked at source tonight; a court's words for Q7b-009 and Q7b-002 (31 March 2028; a Treasury payment more than five business days late); one clause at most, said as Keel's reading since no court has read l.17.
Wed 18 Nov: store; the anchor for the dated count (Delaware once, in Akorn, 2018); it took the target's own collapse, not the market's; the 86% and 25% read in excerpts only.

Wed 18 Nov: 3b or 3e, each risk placed on the part of her money built to bear it; fix the use column: market moves also set the bottom until January 2028 (Table 3 row 6: the bottom to Jan 2028, the top to Jan 2031, then her flexibility), so never market risk on the top and her flexibility alone.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e aha (a judge who reads l.17 as a MAC has it backwards: a US default, the most market-wide event, is on the list); fix the line, which covers only reason 2: say a flow the plan does not own fails to arrive (the 2028 deposit, a Treasury's payment, Q3b-034) against the numbers move; never only two things can break the plan (Q109-033); untested on a cold reader.
Wed 18 Nov: store only; the parallel breaks under its own disanalogy (a company's earnings over years against a share index on one day); its 8p figures are right ($95,000 to $105,000, all ten paid).
Wed 18 Nov: store only; one more Delaware no after Akorn, a fraud case, not a market one; feeds row 22's dated count.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e and Table 3: in AB Stable the carve-out held and the seller still lost because it reacted, so a market carve-out protects only a party that does not react; pairs l.17 with Table 3's Never cells (a bond or fund sold early; a forced sale; the payments), checked in exhibits/tables.md; Table 3 is the report's, never a new rule (CANON A34); row 21 merged here.
Wed 18 Nov: twin of row 20 (two clauses, two jobs); carry its caveat to row 20: the IPS carries only l.17, and the Never cells are the report's Table 3.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e wording guard only: Delaware let a buyer walk away on a MAE once, in Akorn (2018), dated to the cases read through 2021; the count past 2021 is unverified and the one 2026 secondary miscites Akorn, so never exactly once in 25 years.

Wed 18 Nov: store or 3d; the use column is unclear about who would reopen: it is Laura, not co-sponsors; say that after the move her stated figures are owned (NUMBERS 4: certain after the move), so a slump leaves nothing to reopen; the 9% are targets' own MAEs over months, not market falls.

Wed 18 Nov: store; markets pay for a promise hard to leave and its maker pays with a lower price, an association in one 2010 working paper, not a cause; if used, the price is NUMBERS 4's what certainty costs the gift, never Q7-030's void figures.

Wed 18 Nov: store or 3d; fix the use: co-sponsors can lean on the stated figures because they are owned in Treasuries after the move (NUMBERS 4), and l.17 adds that no downturn is a reason to change; never that the bottom is stated before the move.

Wed 18 Nov: 3a or 3e reference: the UCC's Neither is a rise or a collapse in the market in itself a justification, checked at source tonight; the ten are a fixed promise and the plan holds Treasuries to keep it; sales law, not Laura's promise, said once; rows 27 and 29 merged here.
Wed 18 Nov: twin of row 26 (a second US authority, read only in a court's quotation).

Wed 18 Nov: 3a reference beside row 26 (Posner: If such a gamble fails, the result is not force majeure); fix the use: the ten are Treasuries maturing just before each payment, five bonds and five iBond funds that pay their net asset value, never Treasuries that pay fixed dollars on the payment dates.
Wed 18 Nov: twin of row 26 (a third US authority: the 2008 downturn excused nothing); adds only that hardship excuses only if written in the contract, which l.17 does in two events.
Wed 18 Nov: store or a reference: English law agrees even after 2008-09; say three legal systems agree only with Taiwan's narrow exception named (rows 31 and 33).

Wed 18 Nov: RESIDENCY store; Taiwan's Supreme Court asks whether a change lies within the risk the contract's terms can bear, a client-knowledge line at most; Taiwan law is outside the case's scope, never legal advice; row 36 merged here.
Wed 18 Nov: store only; a High Court view the Supreme Court left unreviewed, never stated as Taiwan's law.

Wed 18 Nov: RESIDENCY store; in Taiwan a crash can be argued to reopen a building contract's fixed price, beside Q103-022 to Q103-025; read through one article, the remand's outcome unknown; never for the ten payments.
Wed 18 Nov: store only; one arbitral use of change of circumstances on a currency shock, set aside on procedure; a derivative sold to firms, nothing like Laura's plan.
Wed 18 Nov: RESIDENCY store; adds one district court to Q103-023 (a blanket exclusion void, a specific price-risk clause stands); never legal advice.
Wed 18 Nov: twin of row 31 (normal risk is the same test); adds only the 1955 land-rent scale.
Wed 18 Nov: twin of row 8 (the plan watches payments, not values); never let years not months suggest the plan measures a fall's size.

Wed 18 Nov: twin of Q7-031 once fixed: by 2031 the deposit reason has closed (31 March 2028), so co-sponsors rely on one exit, a Treasury payment more than five business days late, not two; the MAC disanalogy is already in row 1's critique.

Wed 18 Nov: the card's 3e wording note, twin of rows 3, 14 and 20; carry its guards: never call l.17 a MAC clause (it works like a merger agreement's carve-out), never only two things can break the plan (Q109-033), never a new rule (CANON A34); its 99 in 100 waits on row 3's check.
